title.narrative: Provision of multisector services in Health, Nutrition, GP/CP/GBV, and S/NFIs to IDPs affected by famine in Krenek and Habila locality of West Darfur.

description.narrative: ltpgtSince the outbreak of conflict in Sudan in April 2023, over 10.4 million people have been forcibly displaced, including 8 million internally and 2.2 million who have sought refuge in neighboring countries. The conflict has led to massive displacements, significant disruptions in market systems and supply chains, and the collapse of health systems. Movement restrictions and inaccessibility to farmlands have caused a rapid depletion of local supplies and limited livelihood opportunities.ltbrgtThe resulting scarcity of health and nutrition care, reduced crop production, and soaring prices for food, commodities, and services have exacerbated the vulnerability of the affected population, particularly women, girls, and children. This has led to increased protection risks, such as a surge in mental health issues and gender-based violence. Additionally, the breakdown of family structures has resulted in a rise in unaccompanied and separated children, further intensifying the crisis.ltbrgtThis project is designed to address the impact of key drivers of humanitarian needs and reduce the risk of famine in identified priority areas, based on the findings of the Famine Review Committee. The project will provide an integrated multisectoral response in Health, Nutrition, Protection, and Shelter and NFIs to IDPs affected by famine in Krenik and Habila localities (IPC 4).ltbrgtThe intervention will support the reactivation of 2 health facilities in Habila and 3 health facilities in Krenik, as well as establish 2 mobile health teams (one in each locality) to reach those without access to healthcare. The project aims to improve access to integrated primary health care (PHC) services for 136,036 individuals, including maternal and child health services, free curative health care consultations, immunizations, and the provision of essential drugs and non-medical supplies.ltbrgtThe Nutrition services will focus on the treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) without medical complications and provide referral support for SAM cases with medical complications. Additionally, the program will address Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) in children under 5 and in PLW through TSFP. The initiative will also incorporate community-based interventions with the support of Community Nutrition Volunteers, aligning with the Nutrition Cluster consensus to effectively respond to the needs of the famine-affected population. ltbrgtAdditionally, the vulnerable population will receive Non-Food Items (NFIs) to protect them from environmental and social risks and improve their living conditions. A total of 11,300 people will receive essential items such as blankets, sleeping mats, mosquito nets, and utensils. In Habila locality, 650 IDP households will be provided with emergency shelter.ltbrgtThe distribution of these shelter items aims to offer critical protection from damage and natural hazards, addressing immediate shelter needs while also reducing the risk of gender-based violence (GBV). The distribution process will prioritize maintaining dignity, incorporating safeguarding measures, and ensuring accountability. An integrated protection activities for GBV, CP, and general protection will be carried out to help manage cases, reduce the risks, and support the recovery of survivors. ltbrgtThe consortium partners (WR, CDF, SORR, HOPE) bring prior experience in Habila and Krenek localities. Given the complex conflict dynamics in West Darfur, the consortium will, in consultation with local authorities and community leaders at both the locality and state levels, adopt a conflict-sensitive approach to mitigate ethnic tensions during project implementation. This balanced approach will ensure equitable resource allocation and foster social cohesion among the targeted populations.ltbrgtAdditionally, cross-cutting themes such as protection mainstreaming, disability inclusion, gender mainstreaming, and accountability to affected populations are fully integrated into the project to ensure safe and dignified programming.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
